issues.claim: R3-08 (b) keeps VV56-r2-06 a blocker because 'every restoration that re-cuts … would draw new elements as patched repairs they never had' — the claim's first case being the restoring event's own re-cut for its new occupants. The ruled mechanism reads each element's peak from its entry week, for an element a re-cut mints ('a restoring event's included') 'that change's effective week' (V06 §3.23 (3), l. 3409–3412; decayPeak's `since`, l. 3382; V03 §5.6 (2) (b), l. 2697–2701). At the restoring event's week the level is still the run's: a `reoccupy` under its `repair` Works reads L × (1 − f(w)) from the Works' start, L the level the week before (V06 §3.23 (3)). So an element that re-cut mints (a new occupant's partition, door, furniture) is drawn DAMAGED from its first week (a `decayed` building's level lies in [1/3, 2/3]; V11's partition range 0.36–0.66) and then REPAIRED in patch material for ever once the Works lowers the level past it, its peak since entry being L; only a restoration with no Works escapes. V06 §3.23 (3) itself says only elements added 'after' the damage left are never drawn repaired, but the bars and edge rows assert the restoring re-cut's case: T-V6-76 (b) 'a reoccupy from derelict with a re-cut …: 0 added elements drawn repaired' (V06 l. 4143), V06 §3.21's decay row 'the added elements drawn as built' (l. 3274), V03 §3.13's damage-layer row 'an element a restoring re-cut … adds → drawn as built, never repaired' (l. 2094) and T-V3-39 (c) 'drawn as built, never patched' (l. 2898). The formula gives the wrong result on the common path (works on by default) and those bars cannot pass on it.
issues.required_change: V06 §3.23 (3), after '… or a wing an `extend` adds at that change's effective week': '— save that an element a restoring event's re-cut mints (V03 §3.11: the new occupants' rooms) enters the plan, for its damage, at the week that restoration ends — its `repair` Works' FINISHED week, or the week a decay run that interrupts it begins; with no Works, the event's effective week — and is drawn as built before that week: no level the restoration lowers damages it or is its peak, so a restoration's new elements are neither damaged nor repaired, and a kept element keeps its peak'; decayPeak's `since` comment (l. 3382) adds 'for an element a restoring re-cut mints, the week that restoration ends'; §3.21's decay row reads 'the added elements drawn as built through the restoration and after it, the kept ones patched'; T-V6-76 (b) adds 'under a `repair` Works, every element the reoccupy's re-cut mints drawn as built in every week of the Works'. Ends: V03 §5.6 (2) (a) adds 'an element is compared with the level only from its entry week ((b); V06 §3.23 (3))', and (b)'s 'that change's effective week (V06 §2.11)' reads 'that change's effective week (V06 §2.11) — for a restoring event's re-cut, the week that restoration ends (V06 §3.23 (3))'; V03 §1b's and §2.5's `planDamage` input cells the same; model §2.6 step 7's 'an element that entered the plan after its damage left never drawn repaired' adds 'nor one a restoring re-cut minted (V06 §3.23 (3))'.

issues.claim: VV34-r2-11's fix makes V03 §5.1 (l. 2458–2460) pick a damaged floor's form by kind: 'a damaged `groundFloor` element takes §8.6's ground-level form (a rotten patch, still walkable) at whatever level it lies, a solid wing's first storey included, and a damaged `upperFloor` element §8.6's hole', its `ruined` look keeping a solid wing's first storey walkable (l. 2465). §8.6, the home of the damaged forms, still picks by position: 'floor area | on any storey above ground level, a hole … the storey below seen through it; at ground level and under it, a rotten patch' (base l. 13964) and 'leaving the ground storey the only one that can be walked' (l. 13975). The first storey of a wing on a solid wing (V03 §3.3's s₀(w) ≥ 1: item 110's shrines and tiers) is above ground level: a hole onto solid fill by §8.6, a walkable patch by V03 and T-V3-39 (d). V03 §13's row (l. 3249) names §8.6 as the other end; it is unwritten (no END line named it; V03's HAND-OFFS).
issues.required_change: §8.6's floor-area row: 'floor area | an `upperFloor` element (V03 §5.6 (1)): a hole: the area filled in `void` under a dense `ink` cross-hatch at α 0.4 (the drop), its edge a broken hairline, the storey below seen through it as `trace` hairlines; a `groundFloor` element — at ground level, under it, or a wing's first storey on a solid wing — a rotten patch in `ground` stipple, still walkable'; the `ruined` sentence (l. 13975) reads 'leaving the ground storey — with a solid wing's first storey — the only one that can be walked'.

issues.claim: V03 counts `storeyGone` per storey 'every `upperFloor` area of which is damaged' (V03 §4.6, l. 2381; §4.5, l. 2294, 'V03 §4.6's `storeyGone` rule'), so the ground storey, whose floors are `groundFloor` and only rot (§8.6), is never 'gone'. V09 §4.21.13 (1), which builds the plan panel's lines, reads '`storeyGone` once every floor area of a storey has fallen' (l. 3652–3653), its `floor` line now saying floors are 'rotten or fallen through' (l. 2187): at level 1 every floor area of the ground storey is damaged, so one builder names the walkable ground storey 'The ground floor is gone' and the other does not (the same for a solid wing's first storey), while V03 §5.6 (7) has one reading feed the panel and the `plan` section. V03 §13's row (l. 3250) names V09 §4.21.13 (1) as the other end; it is unwritten.
issues.required_change: V09 §4.21.13 (1): '(`floor`, and `storeyGone` once every `upperFloor` area of a storey shows damaged (V03 §4.6's rule) — "the upper floor is gone")'; T-V9-86 adds 'a `ruined` building at level 1 shows no `storeyGone` line for its ground storey'.

issues.claim: Round 3 rewrote `PlanDamage.own`'s comment (V03 l. 2682): 'V06's decayLevel(doc, lineage, week) alone; 0 for a standing building outside a run (V06 §3.23 (2))'. A building reoccupied under a `repair` Works is standing and outside its run (the run lasts 'until a restoring event', V06 §3.23 (1)), yet its level is L × (1 − f(w)) until FINISHED (V06 §3.23 (3)) — the weeks in which (b)'s repaired elements leave. The field's definition is right; the gloss names the wrong value for that case.
issues.required_change: V03 §5.6 (2), the `own` comment: 'V06's decayLevel(doc, lineage, week) alone; 0 for a standing building outside a run and any restoration (V06 §3.23 (2)–(3))'.
